newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says minister resigned over dispute with PM.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says minister resigned over dispute with PM.

text.p: Jordan's Communications and Postal Affairs Minister Jamal Sarayrah resigned over "personal" differences with Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti, a cabinet minister said on Monday.
"The resignation was for purely personal reasons over the jurisdictions granted to the prime minister," Information Minister Marwan Muasher told reporters.
"Kabariti had considerations relating to the welfare of citzens and the cabinet, which Jamal Sarayrah did not agree with and so decided to resign," he said.
Officials said the conflict came to a head last week when Kabariti disregarded Sarayrah's choice of acting minister during the minister's absence from the country to attend a conference.
They said Sarayrah submitted his resignation letter to Kabariti's private secretary on Saturday and then decided to remove himself from the public eye.

He leaked his resignation to a newspaper that quoted him as saying Kabariti's style of running the cabinet and his condescending and arrogant attitude towards his ministerial team was behind his breaking ranks.
Mediation efforts by the Speaker of Parliament, Saed Hayel Srour, deputies and ministers have failed to make Sarayrah change his mind, officials said.
Kabariti regretted the resignation, had "high regard for him on the personal and professional levels" and valued his work at the ministry, Muasher added.
The resignation would be submitted to the cabinet for deliberation before a decision was taken on it, he said.
Businessmen dismissed the impact on plans to privatise the profitable state telecommunications body, which the minister was directing as part of an overall privatisation programme.

They said the move to turn over a 26 percent stake in the telecommunications body to a strategic partner by end of 1997 was part of an IMF and World Bank strategy which Jordan was already undertaking to step up the pace of economic reforms.
